blocks.text: **The problem.** Reverse an array of characters `s` **in place**: modify the input array, using O(1) extra memory.

blocks.alt: Reversing h, e, l, l, o. The recursive idea: swap the two ends, h and o, then reverse what's left between them, e, l, l, the same way. Each call swaps one pair and hands the middle to the next call, until the middle is empty or a single letter.

elements.text: swap the ends, then reverse the middle — the same problem, two smaller
elements.originalText: swap the ends, then reverse the middle — the same problem, two smaller

blocks.text: The idea: a smaller copy of the same problem

Reversing `s[left..right]` means swapping the two end letters and then reversing `s[left + 1..right − 1]` — which is the same problem on a range two letters shorter. The base case is a range with zero or one letters: nothing to do. Recursion expresses that in three lines — but watch the memory: n/2 calls pile up on the call stack, which breaks the O(1) memory rule.

blocks.caption: Each call swaps the two ends and passes the middle to the next call.

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(n)** — n/2 frames on the call stack. Correct, but the problem asks for O(1) extra memory, and 100,000 letters would mean 50,000 frames: a stack overflow in Python.
The recursion is a **tail call** — nothing happens after it — so it turns straight into a loop: the parameters become two variables that move inwards.
**Time O(n), space O(1).** The same steps without the call stack. This is the general lesson: a tail-recursive function always becomes a loop by turning its parameters into variables.

rows.timeWhy: The same **n/2 swaps** in a loop.

items: **Even and odd lengths** — with an odd length the middle letter stays put.
**Long input** — the recursive version runs out of stack in Python around 1,000 frames by default.
**Reverse Linked List** — the recursive version reverses the rest, then hooks the head on the end (Linked List course).
**Valid Palindrome** — compare the ends moving inwards instead of swapping them.
**Reverse Words in a String** — reverse the whole string, then each word.
